import pandas as pd
import numpy as np


def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    target_snapshot = inputs["target_snapshot"].copy()
    cdc_events = inputs["cdc_events"].copy()
    watermark = inputs["watermark"].copy()
    
    # Extract the watermark high_ts value
    high_ts = watermark["high_ts"].iloc[0]
    
    # Filter CDC events: keep only events with event_ts > high_ts
    new_events = cdc_events[cdc_events["event_ts"] > high_ts].copy()
    
    # If no new events, return the target snapshot unchanged
    if new_events.empty:
        return {"new_snapshot": target_snapshot}
    
    # Per product_id, select the latest event by (event_ts DESC, event_seq DESC)
    # This ensures deterministic tie-breaking
    new_events = new_events.sort_values(
        by=["product_id", "event_ts", "event_seq"],
        ascending=[True, False, False]
    )
    latest_events = new_events.drop_duplicates(subset=["product_id"], keep="first")
    
    # Separate deletes from upserts
    deletes = latest_events[latest_events["op"] == "D"]
    upserts = latest_events[latest_events["op"].isin(["I", "U"])]
    
    # Build the new snapshot
    # Start with the current target snapshot
    new_snapshot = target_snapshot.copy()
    
    # Remove products that have delete events
    if not deletes.empty:
        delete_product_ids = set(deletes["product_id"].values)
        new_snapshot = new_snapshot[~new_snapshot["product_id"].isin(delete_product_ids)]
    
    # Upsert products (insert new or update existing)
    if not upserts.empty:
        # Create the upsert dataframe with the required schema
        upsert_data = upserts[["product_id", "name", "price"]].copy()
        upsert_data["last_event_ts"] = upserts["event_ts"].values
        
        # Remove existing products that are being upserted
        upsert_product_ids = set(upsert_data["product_id"].values)
        new_snapshot = new_snapshot[~new_snapshot["product_id"].isin(upsert_product_ids)]
        
        # Concatenate with upserts and ensure column order matches target schema
        new_snapshot = pd.concat(
            [new_snapshot, upsert_data],
            ignore_index=True,
            sort=False
        )
    
    # Ensure columns are in the correct order and types
    new_snapshot = new_snapshot[["product_id", "name", "price", "last_event_ts"]]
    new_snapshot = new_snapshot.reset_index(drop=True)
    
    # Ensure dtypes match the input schema
    new_snapshot["product_id"] = new_snapshot["product_id"].astype("int64")
    new_snapshot["name"] = new_snapshot["name"].astype("object")
    new_snapshot["price"] = new_snapshot["price"].astype("float64")
    new_snapshot["last_event_ts"] = new_snapshot["last_event_ts"].astype("datetime64[us]")
    
    return {"new_snapshot": new_snapshot}
